q-17836.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224557/assets/6e075462cab65c4070ed285e78d71fb2fafd7bcdcb898957456e83cddbf45c18.png)

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=f(-x)?$
q-17836.worked_solution:
To obtain the graph of $y=f(-x)$ from $y=f(x)$, we need to reflect the graph over the $y$-axis. The resulting graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224557/assets/ed0d31d46df8c973f92ff5b8e23a3aaeeb782fa90c2f5abb75dcf88f2d7b7421.png)

q-78777.name: Question 3
q-78777.problem: The point $Q$ with coordinates $(4,1)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(-x)?$
q-78777.worked_solution:
The transformation $y=f(-x)$ reflects the curve $y=f(x)$ in the $y$-axis.

First, notice that the point $P(4,1)$ lies $4$ units to the *right* from the $y$-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected $4$ units to the *left* from the $y$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224557/assets/7e76fb2b9821c8bb116740381248e16d8331fbfc2cce4314984fe39bbfc723e7.png)

We conclude that the point $(-4,1)$ must lie on the graph of $y=f(-x).$

q-78777.html:
Question 3
?

The point Q with coordinates (4,1) lies on the curve y=f(x). Which of the following points must lie on y=f(−x)?

a
(1,−4)
b
(−4,1)
c
(−1,−4)
d
(−4,−1)
e
(4,−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The transformation y=f(−x) reflects the curve y=f(x) in the y-axis.

First, notice that the point P(4,1) lies 4 units to the right from the y-axis. So, under the action of the transformation, this point will be reflected 4 units to the left from the y-axis.

We conclude that the point (−4,1) must lie on the graph of y=f(−x).
q-78777.knowledge_point: Finding a Point that Lies on a Transformed Function
